steps: Rinse out food, sugary beverage, or dairy residue with a little water.
Air dry the item to prevent mold and contamination of paper/cardboard.
Flatten plastic bottles, aluminum cans, and cardboard boxes to save bin space.
Deposit in the dry blue recycling bin or drop off at a local recycling facility.
dos: Do keep plastics, clean cardboard, newspapers, and tin cans dry.
Do keep bottle caps attached to bottles if accepted locally.
Do bundle clean paper sheets together.
donts: Don't put greasy pizza boxes or oil-stained cardboard in recycling.
Don't include plastic bags or shrink wrap unless accepted separately.
Don't mix broken window glass or mirrors with bottle glass.
disposal_guide.environmental_impact: Reduces virgin resource extraction, saves up to 95% energy compared to making new aluminum/plastic, and cuts carbon footprint.
disposal_guide.decomposition_time: Cardboard: 2 months | Aluminum: 200-500 years | Plastic Bottle: 450 years | Glass: 1 million+ years

notes: Rinsed clear water bottle from gym.

disposal_guide.primary_action: Home Composting or Municipal Organic Digestion
steps: Drain any excess soup, curry, or liquid before disposing.
Remove all plastic wrappers, stickers, or rubber bands.
Place into a green biodegradable bag or directly in the green organic bin.
Cover the bin tightly to prevent fruit flies and unwanted odors.
dos: Do include fruit peels, vegetable scraps, leftover food, and eggshells.
Do use newspaper lining or certified compostable bags.
Do mix brown dry leaves if composting at home to balance nitrogen.
donts: Don't mix plastic containers, foil, cutlery, or toothpicks.
Don't put pet feces or sanitary waste in the organic bin.
Don't pour large quantities of cooking oil directly into the bin.
disposal_guide.environmental_impact: Diverts methane-generating organics from landfills and enriches soil with nutrient-dense humus.
disposal_guide.decomposition_time: 2 weeks to 6 months depending on temperature and aeration

disposal_guide.primary_action: Isolate & Hand Over to Authorized E-Waste / Hazardous Center
steps: Never throw in general trash bins or incinerate.
Tape the terminals of lithium or button batteries with clear electrical tape.
Store in a sturdy, non-metallic, dry container away from sunlight and children.
Drop off at designated electronic recycling kiosks, battery bins, or toxic drop-off events.
dos: Do keep broken CFL bulbs inside a sealed plastic container to capture mercury vapor.
Do handle corroded batteries with rubber gloves.
Do wipe device memory before sending electronics for recycling.
donts: Don't crush, puncture, or submerge batteries in water.
Don't pour paint, bleach, or solvents down the household drain.
Don't mix hazardous materials together in a single open bag.
disposal_guide.environmental_impact: Prevents toxic heavy metals (lead, cadmium, mercury, lithium) from leaching into groundwater and agricultural soil.
disposal_guide.decomposition_time: Non-biodegradable; toxins remain permanently hazardous without high-temperature treatment

notes: Exhausted AA remote control batteries taped safely.

disposal_guide.primary_action: Secure Bagging for Waste-to-Energy or Controlled Landfill
steps: Ensure the item is free of rotting food or wet organic fluids.
Wrap sharp broken ceramic fragments in newspaper for sanitation worker safety.
Place into a sturdy trash bag and tie securely.
Deposit in the non-recyclable municipal dry waste bin.
dos: Do wrap broken pottery, multi-layer snack wrappers, and old sponges.
Do keep the dry trash separate from wet composting streams.
Do minimize using single-use non-recyclable multi-layered packaging.
donts: Don't dump wet organic food or slurry into the dry bin.
Don't place batteries, electronics, or medical waste here.
Don't burn dry domestic waste openly.
disposal_guide.environmental_impact: Managed under municipal RDF (Refuse-Derived Fuel) or engineered sanitary landfills.

steps: Check the recycling resin code on the bottom of the item (numbers 1 through 7).
Separate composite materials (e.g., detach paper label from plastic cup).
If mostly organic food material, discard into Green Bin.
If clean recyclable rigid plastic/metal/paper, discard into Blue Bin.
If containing circuit boards, wires, or batteries, treat as Red Bin Hazardous.
dos: Do perform a visual test: is it organic, clean paper, metal, or electronic?
Do ask your local municipality when in doubt.
donts: Don't guess randomly and throw non-recyclables into the blue bin (wishcycling).
Don't dispose hazardous materials in ordinary trash.
disposal_guide.environmental_impact: Careful sorting prevents batch contamination at municipal recycling facilities.
